objects: The unchanged causal P(t)=sum_n Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) H(t-log n), H=kappa*kappa, and the literal complete self-convolution S=P*P. Every prime power and both complete histories remain. S is not identified with the original Mobius quadratic or a single parity energy.

supplier.gamma: The separately reviewed external Arb sign certificate and xi reality/IVT give some actual critical zero 1/2+i gamma with14<gamma<15. No simplicity or first-zero claim.
supplier.pole: For its finite multiplicity m>=1, Phat has simple residue -m K_H(i gamma), so Shat=Phat^2 has leading double-pole coefficient A=m^2 K_H(i gamma)^2>0.
supplier.authority: Source-exact analytic composition with a rigorous external interval supplier, not a new Lean theorem or compiler certificate.

claim: limsup_(t->infinity) S(t)/t >= A and liminf_(t->infinity) S(t)/t <= -A. Extended limits are allowed. Thus the same inequalities hold with the smaller positive explicit certified_A_lower_exact. These are LOWER bounds on the size of cofinal positive and negative excursions, not an O(t) upper bound, asymptotic, density or bounded-gap claim.
proof: Fix epsilon in{+1,-1}. If epsilon S(t)<=C t eventually for some C>=0, choose T after that threshold and set u(t)=1_[T,infinity)(C t-epsilon S(t))>=0. The exact causal transform on the original safe half-plane is U(z)=C/z^2-epsilon Shat(z)-E(z), where E(z)=integral_0^T exp(-zt)(C t-epsilon S(t))dt is ENTIRE. No initial history is omitted.

The actual positive-tail Laplace domain is nonempty by the elementary source exponential bound. If its finite abscissa were positive, the positive-Laplace boundary theorem would contradict analyticity of the displayed meromorphic expression at that positive REAL point. Shat is analytic at every positive real point, with the zeta pole at z=1/2 canceled by the actual source. The identity with the actual transform on its integrability half-plane forces any candidate interior nonreal poles removable; this argument does not presuppose RH. If the domain is unbounded below, or the finite abscissa is nonpositive, convergence at every a>0 is immediate. Therefore U is the actual integral for every Re z>0.

Positivity gives |U(a+i gamma)|<=U(a) for every a>0. Since Shat is analytic at0, a^2 U(a)->C. At the certified nonzero critical frequency, C/z^2 and E are analytic, while Shat has leading coefficient A, so a^2 U(a+i gamma)->-epsilon A. Taking limits forces A<=C.

If limsup epsilon S(t)/t<A, select a nonnegative C strictly between that limsup and A (or C=0 if the limsup is negative). This supplies the forbidden eventual bound. Thus limsup epsilon S(t)/t>=A for both signs epsilon, proving the claim.

native_grid.derivative_price: The separately derived quantitative PNT bounds for P and P-prime can be enlarged on the finite initial interval to |P(r)|+|P-prime(r)|<=C exp(r/2-c sqrt(r)) for every r>=0. The source is identically zero near0, so S-prime=P-prime*P with no boundary atom. Since sqrt(u)+sqrt(t-u)>=sqrt(t), |S-prime(t)|<=C^2 t exp(t/2-c sqrt(t)).
native_grid.interpolation: The native mesh has width t_(N+1)-t_N<=2/N. Since exp(t_N/2)=N/sqrt(tau), its S variation is O((1+t_N)exp(-c sqrt(t_N)))=o(1). Consequently an eventual bound epsilon S(t_N)<=C t_N with C<A would extend to epsilon S(t)<C-prime t with some C<C-prime<A for all large real t, contradicting the real-scale result.
native_grid.conclusion: limsup_N S(t_N)/t_N>=A and liminf_N S(t_N)/t_N<=-A. Equivalently, with log N normalization the lower excursion constants are2A and-2A. No moving-cutoff response is replaced by an independent auxiliary source.

target_implication: A constant self-echo bound and an eventual one-sided linear bound with slope below this actual critical-source coefficient are false targets. An all-positive-rate subexponential bound remains compatible with these oscillations and remains OPEN. The estimate supplies no opposing bound at any off-line-zero growth rate and does not close Step4.
new_vs_prior: The previous note excluded only eventual constant one-sided bounds after paying critical visibility. The new comparison retains C/z^2 and yields explicit two-sided linear Omega bounds, including the native grid. It does not infer an unconditional linear oscillation asymptotic from the existence of a critical zero.
